Cabopino is a quiet beach and marina about 5 NM east of Puerto Banús, popular for its natural dunes and calm waters. No license is needed because a professional skipper is included on every charter.

Why choose a no-license boat rental in Cabopino?

Cabopino is one of the quieter coastal spots near Marbella, with a small marina, a sandy beach backed by dunes, and several chiringuitos (beach bars). Renting a boat without a license means you can enjoy the freedom of the sea without the hassle of paperwork. Our charters depart from Puerto Banús, a short 20–30 minute cruise away. The skipper handles everything: navigation, anchoring, and safety. You just bring your sunglasses and swimwear.

Cabopino boat rental no license 2033: prices

Our no-license boat rentals start at €749 for 2 hours on a 12.5m Astondoa 40 (9 pax) or Azimut 39 (11 pax). An 8-hour day charter is €2,299. For a larger group, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) costs €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a free jet ski. All prices include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and IVA. No hidden extras.

Which boats can I rent without a license?

You can rent any boat from our fleet without a license because a skipper is always included. Popular choices for Cabopino trips include the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) for small groups, the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) for a bit more space, and the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) for a luxury experience with a free jet ski. The Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) is ideal for couples or small families.

What is included in the no-license boat rental?

Every charter includes: licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). You do not need to bring anything except towels and sunscreen. The skipper will also provide a cooler with ice.

Cabopino boat rental no license 2033: rules

Spanish law requires a license to operate a boat over 5m or with an engine over 15 HP. However, renting a boat with a licensed skipper is completely legal and does not require you to hold any license. The skipper is responsible for navigation, safety, and compliance with maritime rules. You are free to relax, swim, and enjoy the coast.

How to get to Cabopino from Puerto Banús?

Cabopino is about 5 nautical miles east of Puerto Banús. By boat, it takes 20–30 minutes depending on speed and conditions. The skipper will navigate along the coast, passing Marbella's Golden Mile and the Marbella Marina before reaching Cabopino's small harbour. You can also anchor off the beach and swim ashore.

Best time for a no-license boat trip to Cabopino

The best months are May to October, when sea temperatures range from 18°C to 26°C and winds are light. July and August are peak season, so book at least a week in advance. Morning departures (10:00) offer calm seas, while afternoon trips (15:00) are warmer for swimming.
